messages:
elaine: Quick heads-up — did an initial bring-up for `evoke-v1` embeddings with int4 quantization on Holdout A. Numbers look off compared to float baseline.
kevin: Which split / dataset exactly?
elaine: Holdout A (50k queries, 200k corpus). Baselines: float R@1 81.5%, R@5 92.0. int4 run: R@1 78.3, R@5 90.9. silhouette dropped 0.42 -> 0.33. cluster purity down ~4%.
ranjit: :eyes: can you paste the exact command + config?
elaine: Sure — ran the nightly harness:
```
runeval --model evoke-v1 --quant=int4 --quant-mode=symmetric --norm=None --dataset=holdoutA --batch-size=1024 --seed=42
```
ci-bot: nightly-eval finished | model=evoke-v1 | quant=int4 | dataset=holdoutA | R@1=78.3 | R@5=90.9 | silhouette=0.33
anika: Did you use per-tensor or per-channel quantization? That can matter for attention/MLP weights.
elaine: Default was per-tensor symmetric (we used the shim from the generic quant script). Re-running with per-channel now.
tomas: Also verify the postprocessing — are embeddings L2-normalized before similarity? We had a preproc mismatch last month that looked like quant degradation.
elaine: Good call. First run had no L2 norm (we were comparing raw vectors). I just re-ran with per-channel + L2 norm:
```
runeval --model evoke-v1 --quant=int4 --quant-mode=per-channel --norm=L2 --dataset=holdoutA --batch-size=1024 --seed=42
```
elaine: New numbers: R@1=80.9, R@5=91.8, silhouette=0.40. Still slightly below float R@1 (81.5) but much closer.
kevin: Great. So per-channel + L2 recovers most. Do we need to update the quant recipe?
ranjit: We should add a quick note to the model onboarding doc recommending per-channel quant + L2 for evoke-v1. Also run 3 seeds to be sure (seed variance can be non-trivial).
anika: Agree. Also run a clustering scatter (UMAP/PCA) on a 5k sample and check centroid shifts. Can you push plots to the dashboard?
elaine: Pushed a small report + CSV to internal dashboard: https://tiny.redwood/dash/evoke-int4-holdoutA (internal). Attached sample plots in the report.
tomas: If per-channel solves it reliably, we can add an Optimize rule: prefer per-channel for evoke family and recommend `norm=L2` in the inference pipeline.
elaine: Will run 3 seeds and a longer run over Holdout B tomorrow. For now note: int4 is viable with per-channel + L2, but default per-tensor symmetric + no-norm causes noticeable drop.
kevin: Thanks — add a short summary to the onboarding PR and flag for docs/optimize. :thumbsup:
ranjit: +1
ci-bot: PR check | evoke-onboard-quant updated with evaluation note (CI link: https://ci.redwood/evoke/1234)
